feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (development simulator, 60 trials) ended every run off track with progress 0.10 to 0.15, exactly one line-loss event per run, and max_error of about 0.062 m, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. rms_error (0.025 to 0.029 m) and steering_oscillation (0.08 to 0.14) were both low, so the baseline drifted steadily toward one edge rather than weaving. This candidate tests the drift hypothesis (H1) by raising ki from 0.05 to 0.3 so the integral can cancel the fixed left/right motor mismatch, and raising kp from 2.0 to 2.5 to tighten tracking. Geometry, base_speed, kd, and line_loss are unchanged, so any change in the result can be attributed to the gains. The design is valid and not obviously broken: the integral clamp of +/-2 bounds the windup contribution, and kd is unchanged, so no new instability source is introduced. The bar here is validity, and this is an early iteration with ten left, so the race is the most useful next step.

What to do next depends on the race. (1) If progress rises and max_error falls clearly below 0.06 but the robot still leaves the line, the sensor span is probably too narrow: the outer sensors at x = +/-0.03 go dark near 0.043 m offset, so the robot is effectively blind before it reaches the off-track limit. Widen the span to x = +/-0.04 and keep the gains. (2) If line_loss_events stays at 1 and the failure happens on bend entries (s-bend or slalom), the robot is likely arriving too fast for the correction. Lower base_speed to about 1.3 before touching the gains again. (3) If steering_oscillation rises sharply with kp, reduce kp back toward 2.0 and raise kd to 0.2 to damp it, rather than raising ki further.
requested_changes: If the robot still leaves the line with max_error near 0.06 m, widen the outer sensors to x = -0.04 and +0.04 (keeping the other three sensors) so line loss is detected before the off-track limit.

If failures cluster on bend entries (s-bend or slalom), lower base_speed from 1.6 to about 1.3 before changing the gains again, since the iteration 0 baseline showed one line-loss event per run that looks like a late reaction at speed.

If steering_oscillation rises well above the iteration 0 range (0.08 to 0.14) with kp = 2.5, set kp back to 2.0 and raise kd from 0.1 to 0.2 to damp the swing, keeping ki = 0.3 to cancel the motor-mismatch drift.
